## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

X8 in four fascicles is [員珂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%93%A1%E7%8F%82)'s late-Ming triple-translation collation (*huìyì* 會譯) of the three extant Chinese versions of the *Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra*: [T670](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0327) (Liú-Sòng [求那跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85), 4 fascicles), [T671](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0328) (Northern Wèi [菩提流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF), 10 fascicles), and [T672](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0329) (Tang [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80), 7 fascicles). The book is structurally remarkable: [員珂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%93%A1%E7%8F%82) takes [求那跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85)'s shortest version as the principal text — running it as the head-line — and inserts the parallel passages from [菩提流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) and [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) as sub-lines below the head-line, allowing the reader to compare the three Chinese translations *in situ*.

**Abstract**

The work is one of the principal late-Míng synthetic *Laṅkāvatāra* productions, paralleling the contemporaneous *Laṅkāvatāra* commentaries by [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) ([KR6i0343](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0343)) and [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) ([KR6i0345](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0345), [KR6i0346](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0346)). [員珂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%93%A1%E7%8F%82)'s *huìyì* serves a different function from those commentaries: it is not exegetical but textual-comparative, providing the late-Míng reader (Chán or Tiāntái) with a single book in which the three Chinese versions could be checked against one another. As such, X8 is the principal Chinese precursor of the kind of synoptic critical edition that modern philology has produced.

[員珂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%93%A1%E7%8F%82)'s collaboration with the lay official Lù Guāngzǔ 陸光祖 ("Lù Sīkōng Guāngzǔ" in his DILA biography) on the project is also notable — the assistance of an established Wànlì lay literato gave the work the social leverage to be printed and circulated.

Related canonical texts: [KR6i0327](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0327) (T670), [KR6i0328](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0328) (T671), [KR6i0329](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0329) (T672) — the three parent translations.
